question: Who sells or buys causal discovery and causal analysis today, for which decisions, with what claimed guarantees, at what price model, and where does it fail in practice? Which guarantee (accuracy, calibrated uncertainty, abstention, provenance/audit trail, speed, cost) do buyers actually pay for?

schema.kind: product | case study | use case | deployed system (paper) | research for industry | buyer evidence | evaluation evidence | market evidence | market estimate
schema.name: product or use case
schema.method_family: discovery / effect estimation / both / RCA (with a short note on where the graph comes from)
schema.adoption_evidence: customers, funding, case studies; type labelled
schema.failure_or_criticism: with source in the sources list

rows.name: decisionOS (G-Cloud 14 listing)
rows.decision_supported: KPI driver analysis, scenario simulation, pricing/promotion, fairness checks in lending and recruitment
rows.method_family: both (human-guided causal discovery + effect/scenario estimation)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): automatically identifies cause-and-effect relationships for KPIs; 'Accelerating time from data to value 3 to 10 times'. Only contractual guarantees on the page are service-level: 99% monthly uptime, 5% service credit per 4h+ outage. No guarantee of model accuracy.
rows.pricing_model: claim (vendor) list price: GBP 240,000 per licence per year; 2-week free trial on example data only
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): $45m Series A (Dorilton, Molten Ventures), Aviva and TIAA named as users, revenue growth >500% after leaving stealth in Jan 2021
rows.failure_or_criticism: Observed: causaLens homepage (read today) no longer mentions decisionOS; it sells LLM 'Digital Workers' (see C02). Case studies give value figures without accuracy metrics (see C03).

rows.name: Digital Workers (Blueprints, Digital Worker Factory, System of Work)
rows.decision_supported: automating repetitive knowledge workflows; 'causal-driven answers'
rows.method_family: unknown (marketing says workers 'reason via causation'; no method stated)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): '5x ROI in year one'; financial services: 'guaranteed ROI and audit-ready reliability'; compliance tagline 'Always Accurate'; governance layer with audit trails and automated evaluation
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): logos/quotes from Johnson & Johnson, McCann Worldgroup, DANA Indonesia, Syneos Health, Cisco, Croud
rows.failure_or_criticism: No evidence offered for 'Always Accurate' or guaranteed ROI on the page. The pivot itself is a signal: the best-known causal-AI pure play now leads with LLM agents plus audit trails, not with causal discovery.

rows.name: Manufacturing root-cause case study (commodity manufacturer)
rows.decision_supported: find components behind machine instabilities (tens of faults per week) to cut downtime
rows.method_family: both (time-series causal model + RCA engine; whether the graph was learned or specified is not stated)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'over $15 million through reduced production downtime'; no accuracy, precision or baseline
rows.adoption_evidence: case study type: vendor-hosted, anonymised customer ($20bn commodity manufacturer)
rows.failure_or_criticism: No method detail or metric; value figure not verifiable.

rows.name: CauseWay / PathWay (incl. PathWay for Rail - Delay Attribution)
rows.decision_supported: delay attribution under railway rules (DAPR); root causes and what-if scenarios
rows.method_family: both (causal knowledge graphs; LLM-assisted causal discovery per analyst interview)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): causal reasoning gives better operational decisions than summaries; no accuracy figure. Rail product covers about 40% of attribution scenarios at first deployment.
rows.pricing_model: not public; 'priced below' traditional enterprise projects; tools licensable
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): built with Great Western Railway, entering production June 2026; IBM watsonx integration. second-hand: analyst piece names no customers
rows.failure_or_criticism: Analyst piece is an interview with the CEO; no independent results.

rows.name: Causely causal reasoning platform
rows.decision_supported: identify root cause of service incidents and feed 'deterministic causal context' to AI agents (MCP server)
rows.method_family: RCA (live causal model of services, dependencies and 'known failure paths'; construction method not published)
rows.uses_llm: unknown internally; designed as context for LLM agents
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'zero hallucinations', '100% fault accuracy', -63% time to answer, -48% tokens. reported (vendor-authored arXiv 2605.18327): on a 24-microservice OpenTelemetry demo with injected faults, 4 agent setups, diagnosis accuracy 75% -> 100% with Causely, time-to-diagnosis -63%, tokens -60%, cost per run -57%
rows.pricing_model: claim (vendor): Professional $2,000/month for up to 500 services; Enterprise custom; 30-day trial
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): $8.8M seed (645 Ventures lead, June 2023), >$11M total; Gartner 'Cool Vendor for AI in IT Operations' (Dec 2025); logos incl. Unity, Cisco
rows.failure_or_criticism: Self-evaluation on one demo application with injected faults; no independent benchmark found.

rows.name: Davis causal AI / Dynatrace Intelligence root-cause analysis
rows.decision_supported: group anomalies into one problem, rank root-cause contributors, drive automated remediation
rows.method_family: RCA (fault-tree analysis over the Smartscape dependency topology; topology is declared/observed, not learned by discovery)
rows.uses_llm: separate natural-language assistant; RCA itself not LLM
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'answers, not guesses' from deterministic causal AI; docs speak of the 'most probable root cause'; no accuracy number
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand (Omdia analyst, Feb 2026): differentiation resonates with enterprises
rows.failure_or_criticism: Docs admit duplicate problems for the same root cause at detection time (accepted to keep alerts fast), fixed merge windows (90 min, 5 min). Analyst: needs proof that Smartscape maps dependencies customers cannot see elsewhere; too early to judge autonomous operation.

rows.name: Watchdog Root Cause Analysis
rows.decision_supported: find originating service and user impact of an incident
rows.method_family: RCA (causal links between symptoms across services; method not published)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'often solves in minutes' what takes hours or days; no accuracy
rows.pricing_model: bundled with APM (no separate price read)
rows.adoption_evidence: case study type: one customer quote (Cvent) in press release, April 2022
rows.failure_or_criticism: No independent measurement.

rows.name: Bits AI SRE / Bits Investigation
rows.decision_supported: autonomous incident investigation: propose root-cause hypotheses, test each with telemetry queries
rows.method_family: RCA (LLM agent hypothesis-test loop, not a causal graph)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'decrease time to resolution by up to 95%'; internal benchmark of labelled real incidents scored by an LLM judge aligned with human judgement; no pass rate in text
rows.pricing_model: claim (vendor): about 6.5 AI credits per investigation; $1.00/credit on annual plan, $1.30 on demand (about $6.50-8.45 per investigation)
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): benchmark labelled by 'hundreds of teams'
rows.failure_or_criticism: Vendor blog admits earlier versions returned wrong root causes when distracted by suspicious signals and stopped at surface causes (OOM kills instead of large payloads).

rows.name: Intelligent RCA (iRCA), preview
rows.decision_supported: separate probable root cause from cascading symptoms
rows.method_family: RCA (topology graph + 'causal models' + path-based ranking)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): root cause 'in seconds instead of hours', 'high-accuracy'; no numbers, no evaluation described
rows.adoption_evidence: announced Feb 2026 (preview)
rows.failure_or_criticism: No benchmark or method detail.

rows.name: Instana root cause identification (RCI)
rows.decision_supported: rank components most likely responsible for a failure in distributed systems
rows.method_family: RCA (Beta-Binomial health model over request traces and dependency topology; Pearl-style framing; no training)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported (IBM authors, arXiv 2502.18240): root cause identified in about 90% of cases in internal production-scale experiments; authors estimate MTTR reduction of at least 80%; reports low confidence when telemetry is sparse instead of guessing
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: GA planned early 2025; internal case: faulty networking switch found in <5 min vs >12 h manual
rows.failure_or_criticism: Internal experiments only; no external benchmark.

rows.name: Groot event-graph RCA
rows.vendor: large e-commerce company (authors' description: >185M active buyers/year)
rows.decision_supported: root cause of production incidents across about 5,000 services
rows.method_family: RCA (rule-based event causality graph; SRE-written rules, not learned)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported: 952 labelled production incidents over 15 months, 78% top-1, 95% top-3
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: deployed and used by the SRE team
rows.failure_or_criticism: Rules must be maintained by engineers; accuracy is in-house.

rows.name: Telecom alarm root-cause discovery (HPCI + CPBE) and EvoCause
rows.vendor: authors overlapping with Huawei telecom work (affiliations not shown on abs pages read)
rows.decision_supported: find root-cause alarms in real-time alarm streams
rows.method_family: discovery (Hawkes process + CI tests to learn alarm causal graph) then RCA; EvoCause: LLM edits a PC graph using past expert diagnoses
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported (EvoCause, arXiv 2607.27290): from PC start, Node F1 +11.59, Case EM +9.40 on synthetic data; on TeleRCA (485,681 production alarm events) replacing alarm titles with anonymous IDs lowers Node F1 by 6.12 and Case EM by 8.04 points. HPCI (arXiv 2105.03092): 'significant improvement' over baselines, no numbers on abs page
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: TeleRCA comes from a production telecom network; no deployment described on pages read
rows.failure_or_criticism: EvoCause depends on alarm names (semantic leakage of the same kind our Causal-Copilot name-swap test measures).

rows.name: Model-monitoring 'root cause analysis'
rows.decision_supported: why a deployed model's performance or drift changed
rows.method_family: not causal (feature attribution, distribution comparison, data-integrity checks)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): actionable insights; the article does not claim causal inference
rows.adoption_evidence: n/a
rows.failure_or_criticism: Included to mark the boundary: 'RCA' in ML monitoring is attribution, not causal analysis.

rows.name: DoWhy graphical causal model (gcm) module: RCA of outliers and distribution changes
rows.decision_supported: attribute anomalies and KPI shifts to causal mechanisms (Shapley-based)
rows.method_family: both (effect/attribution given a graph; structure learning available)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): used internally by teams 'ranging from' Supply Chain to AWS; no accuracy
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): internal Amazon use; DoWhy open-source library
rows.failure_or_criticism: Graph source for RCA not specified in the post.

rows.name: End-to-end causal attribution framework for supply-chain operations
rows.decision_supported: root-cause attribution, intervention and counterfactual analysis for a supply-chain KPI
rows.method_family: discovery (PC on observational data) + effect estimation (DoWhy GCM SCMs)
rows.uses_llm: partly (an LLM-guided DAG is one baseline)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported (KDD 2025 Workshop on AI for Supply Chain, abstract): DAGs validated by falsification tests, SCMs by mechanism/fit checks; 'more robust and nuanced attribution' than rule-based models; no numbers in abstract
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: applied to a supply-chain KPI using representative metrics
rows.failure_or_criticism: Abstract only; no graph accuracy reported. One of few documented commercial uses where the learned graph itself is relied on.

rows.name: Responsible AI dashboard: causal analysis component
rows.decision_supported: effect of a feature on an outcome; which cohorts benefit from a treatment
rows.method_family: effect estimation (EconML double ML; requires all confounders observed)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): DML gives small MSE, asymptotic normality and confidence intervals; discovery delegated to Causica
rows.pricing_model: part of Azure ML (no separate price read)
rows.adoption_evidence: not stated
rows.failure_or_criticism: Assumes no unobserved confounding; no discovery.

rows.name: ShowWhy (no-code causal analysis incl. causal discovery)
rows.decision_supported: no-code exposure analysis, event analysis (synthetic DiD), causal discovery (Causica, NOTEARS, DirectLiNGAM)
rows.method_family: both
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none stated
rows.adoption_evidence: research project
rows.failure_or_criticism: Archived 17 Dec 2025, 'no longer maintained'.

rows.name: Causica (DECI)
rows.decision_supported: end-to-end discovery plus ATE/CATE from observational data
rows.method_family: both
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none stated
rows.adoption_evidence: no releases listed on repo page
rows.failure_or_criticism: Repo notes heavy refactor and removed models.

rows.name: CausalImpact
rows.decision_supported: effect of an intervention on a time series (campaign, policy)
rows.method_family: effect estimation (Bayesian structural time-series synthetic control)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported: posterior intervals for counterfactual (Brodersen et al., arXiv 1506.00356, DOI 10.1214/14-AOAS788)
rows.adoption_evidence: widely used open-source R package (no adoption figure read)
rows.failure_or_criticism: Abs page does not state assumptions; validity rests on control series unaffected by the intervention (standard for the design; not verified from text read).

rows.name: Meridian
rows.decision_supported: cross-channel budget allocation (MMM)
rows.method_family: effect estimation (Bayesian MMM; experiment results as priors)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): calibrate with incrementality experiments as priors; accounts for reach and frequency
rows.pricing_model: free (open source); partner services may cost
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): tested with 'hundreds of brands'; 20+ certified measurement partners; case study Finder
rows.failure_or_criticism: No independent validation in launch post.

rows.name: Robyn
rows.decision_supported: channel efficiency, adstock, saturation, budget allocation (MMM)
rows.method_family: effect estimation (ridge regression + evolutionary hyperparameter search)
rows.uses_llm: Python port translated from R with LLM help (README)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none (project self-described as 'experimental')
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: 1.5k GitHub stars, 434 forks
rows.failure_or_criticism: Python version is beta and may have bugs.

rows.name: CausalML
rows.decision_supported: campaign targeting, personalised engagement (uplift)
rows.method_family: effect estimation (uplift / heterogeneous effects)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none stated
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: about 6.0k GitHub stars; KDD 2021 tutorial on industrial use cases at Microsoft, TripAdvisor, Uber
rows.failure_or_criticism: Repo does not describe Uber's own decisions.

rows.name: Haus (GeoLift experiments, Causal MMM, Causal Attribution, 'Architect' agent)
rows.decision_supported: which channels are incremental; budget reallocation
rows.method_family: effect estimation (geo experiments, synthetic control; MMM anchored on experiments)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): experiments as ground truth for MMM; synthetic-control method '4x more precise' than matched-market tests; 'scientifically sound'
rows.pricing_model: second-hand (Vendr): median annual contract $150,000 (range $132k-168k); tiers Basics/Core/Plus, annual billing
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): $20M led by 01 Advisors (July 2024), Insight Partners; StockX, OluKai mentioned in posts
rows.failure_or_criticism: No independent validation read.

rows.name: Recast (Bayesian MMM + GeoLift)
rows.decision_supported: budget allocation and forecasting
rows.method_family: effect estimation (Bayesian MMM validated by out-of-sample forecasts and lift tests)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): '95%+' predictive accuracy against real outcomes; 'Model holdout accuracy 94.4%'; weekly out-of-sample checks published in platform; 'No vendor smoke screens'
rows.pricing_model: not published; second-hand (CostBench, 40% confidence) estimate $5k-50k/month for the tier; GeoLift about $100/month
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): logos Rocket Money, Canva, Cash App, Hasbro; case studies PODS, Harry's, GetYourGuide
rows.failure_or_criticism: Vendor's own post: no MMM can guarantee being right; recommends backtests and experiment alignment. Forecast accuracy is not effect accuracy.

rows.name: Lifesight unified marketing measurement + Lifesight MCP
rows.decision_supported: budget reallocation, board briefings via Claude/ChatGPT
rows.method_family: effect estimation (MMM + geo incrementality + incrementality-adjusted attribution)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): insight-to-decision 'from weeks to minutes'; every query logged in an audit trail; read-only at launch
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): >300 brands, >$4B marketing spend managed (June 2026)
rows.failure_or_criticism: No accuracy evidence in release.

rows.name: Marketing mix modelling as practised (buyer use case)
rows.decision_supported: channel ROAS and budget split
rows.method_family: effect estimation (observational regression with adstock/saturation)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: second-hand: EMARKETER/TransUnion survey (July 2025): 46.9% of US marketers plan more MMM investment; 27.6% name MMM most reliable; 52% use incrementality tests
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand survey (see claim)
rows.failure_or_criticism: second-hand (news report of preprint arXiv 2608.21128, simulation): standard MMM estimated paid-search ROAS 10.61x vs true 4.20x, 90% interval excluded the truth; geo-experiment structural estimate 4.14x with covering interval. Abstract itself gives no numbers.

rows.name: Statsig (experimentation platform)
rows.decision_supported: ship/no-ship decisions from A/B tests
rows.method_family: effect estimation (randomised experiments)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none read
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand: OpenAI acquisition for $1.1B, announced Sept 2025 (news report)
rows.failure_or_criticism: n/a

rows.name: Eppo (experimentation platform)
rows.decision_supported: A/B test analysis
rows.method_family: effect estimation (randomised experiments)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: none read
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand: Datadog acquisition May 2025, reported about $220M (competitor blog notes no press release on price)
rows.failure_or_criticism: n/a

rows.name: REFS causal AI / Gemini Digital Twins
rows.decision_supported: therapeutic targets and biomarkers from clinical + omics data
rows.method_family: discovery (causal models learned from multi-omics and clinical data, then simulated)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): uncovers 'true disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets'; no accuracy
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): Ono Pharmaceutical partnership for neurology, 2 Sept 2026 (exclusive worldwide option)
rows.failure_or_criticism: No validation evidence in release.

rows.name: Aetion Evidence Platform
rows.decision_supported: regulatory submissions, market access, safety and effectiveness from claims/EHR data
rows.method_family: effect estimation (epidemiologic designs, causal inference)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): 'transparent and reproducible RWE accepted by global regulators, including the FDA and EMA'; 'auditable' platform
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand: Datavant acquisition announced May 2025 (price not stated); investors NEA, Warburg Pincus
rows.failure_or_criticism: No named decisions in release.

rows.name: RCT-DUPLICATE (trial emulation from claims data)
rows.vendor: Brigham and Women's / FDA-funded consortium (Wang, Schneeweiss et al.)
rows.decision_supported: can database studies reproduce RCT conclusions
rows.method_family: effect estimation (target-trial emulation)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: second-hand: 32 trials emulated; correlation of estimates r=0.82 overall, 0.93 where design closely emulated, 0.53 otherwise (JAMA 2023;329(16):1376-85)
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: regulator-funded study
rows.failure_or_criticism: Agreement weak where design elements could not be emulated; sample skewed to cardiovascular trials.

rows.name: PROCOVA (prognostic covariate adjustment with digital twins)
rows.decision_supported: smaller or more powerful Phase 2/3 RCTs
rows.method_family: effect estimation (ANCOVA with ML prognostic score inside a randomised trial)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: regulator: EMA qualification opinion 20 Sept 2022; FDA (per vendor post) said it is a special case of ANCOVA and 'does not appear to deviate' from covariate-adjustment guidance. claim (vendor): reduces sample size 'without creating bias'
rows.adoption_evidence: regulatory qualification (EMA)
rows.failure_or_criticism: FDA: power may be optimistic if covariate-outcome correlation differs from external data.

rows.name: Causaly Bio Graph / research copilot
rows.decision_supported: target identification, indication expansion from literature
rows.method_family: neither discovery-from-data nor estimation: cause-effect relations extracted from text into a knowledge graph (declared knowledge, K)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor): '500M facts and 70M directional relationships'; 'cited' answers; recognises no-answer cases and filters hallucination
rows.adoption_evidence: claim (vendor): logos incl. Ipsen, Teva, UCB, Eisai; earlier rounds $1m seed, $5m Series A, $12m (2021, second-hand)
rows.failure_or_criticism: No accuracy for extracted relations on page.

rows.name: FDA purchase of BayesiaLab licences
rows.decision_supported: let subject-matter experts map causal understanding as diagrams; diagnosis, prediction, simulation
rows.method_family: both (Bayesian networks; expert-drawn plus structure learning)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: requirement (buyer): no extra statistical programming; discrete, nonlinear, nonparametric modelling
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand: RFQ FDA-RFQ-1251846 reported May 2022
rows.failure_or_criticism: n/a

rows.name: Causal DiscoveryBot
rows.decision_supported: alert when a new causal driver of quality loss appears in production data
rows.method_family: discovery (autonomous search for causal factors over production data)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: claim (vendor, via trade press Jan 2024): distinguishes causes from correlations; no accuracy. second-hand (ARC analyst, Sept 2026): time-to-root-cause cut 'from weeks' to under two hours
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand (ARC): Schaeffler and TRUMPF named as customers
rows.failure_or_criticism: No metrics or validation published; analyst urges buyers to demand evidence.

rows.name: Parabole.ai and Ethon (industrial causal AI, per ARC)
rows.decision_supported: root causes and operator guidance
rows.method_family: RCA from declared knowledge (Parabole: graphs from manuals, interviews, Six Sigma heuristics; Ethon: encoded process structure and physics)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: second-hand (ARC): Ethon up to 80% waste reduction, >$10M savings at Siemens; analyst text says causal AI can 'guarantee regulatory compliance' (unsupported)
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand (ARC): Georgia-Pacific (Parabole); Siemens, Lindt, Bosch, Roche (Ethon)
rows.failure_or_criticism: Promotional analyst post; no method or baselines.

rows.name: Causal structure learning for wafer / assembly-line manufacturing
rows.decision_supported: error tracing when domain experts are unavailable
rows.method_family: discovery (hierarchical ensemble with temporal and domain constraints; uncertainty measure)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported: learned structures cross-validated by domain engineers (no metric on pages read); 2016 assembly-line study: experts found results 'promising'
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: Seagate Technology data (NSF award 1952539)
rows.failure_or_criticism: Validation is expert agreement, not ground truth.

rows.name: RCAEval benchmark and 'How far are we' study (evaluation evidence)
rows.decision_supported: how well causal-inference RCA works on microservices
rows.method_family: RCA / discovery evaluation
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported (RCAEval, WWW 2025, preliminary Train Ticket table): metric-based causal methods AC@1 0.09 (RCD), 0.10 (MicroCause), 0.22 (CausalRCA), 0.32 (CIRCA) vs non-causal BARO 0.67. 'How far are we' (arXiv 2408.13729): 9 discovery + 21 RCA methods, none best overall; synthetic results may not transfer
rows.adoption_evidence: n/a
rows.failure_or_criticism: Data-driven causal-discovery RCA underperforms a simple non-causal baseline on these benchmarks.

rows.name: AI incident-response accuracy claims (competitor critique)
rows.decision_supported: vendor selection
rows.method_family: RCA (LLM)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: second-hand: article finds no published precision/recall for production RCA from Rootly; its own claims ('up to 80%' automation, 37% MTTR at one customer) are vendor-hosted or hypothetical
rows.pricing_model: claim (vendor): Rootly about $240-420/user/year; incident.io $45/user/month with on-call
rows.adoption_evidence: n/a
rows.failure_or_criticism: Written by a competitor's CMO; by its own test no vendor RCA accuracy is independently verified.

rows.name: Probabilistic extreme-event attribution (World Weather Attribution protocol)
rows.vendor: World Weather Attribution (KNMI, Imperial and others)
rows.decision_supported: how much climate change altered the probability of an extreme event
rows.method_family: effect estimation (probability ratios from observations and models; not graph discovery)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported (Philip et al. 2020, ASCMO 6:177-203): 8-step standardised protocol; bootstrap (~1,000 resamples) 95% intervals; model-spread inflation in synthesis
rows.adoption_evidence: reported: standard protocol used for rapid attribution studies
rows.failure_or_criticism: n/a

rows.name: Time-series causal discovery in Earth science (PCMCI and others)
rows.decision_supported: teleconnections, drivers of extremes, sea-level rise
rows.method_family: discovery (time-series and spatiotemporal)
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: reported: review of methods, assumptions, evaluation and datasets (arXiv 2404.05746); no accuracy claims on abs page
rows.adoption_evidence: n/a (research use)
rows.failure_or_criticism: Abs page does not discuss validation without ground truth.

rows.name: Causal AI market size estimates
rows.decision_supported: n/a
rows.method_family: n/a
rows.claimed_guarantee_or_accuracy: second-hand: MarketsandMarkets (Dec 2024) USD 56.2M in 2024 -> USD 456.8M by 2030, CAGR 41.8%, BFSI largest vertical; theCUBE Research (Mar 2025) >$1B by 2030 at 41% CAGR
rows.adoption_evidence: second-hand: Dataiku/Databricks survey of 400 senior AI professionals (June 2023) charts 'Causal AI' at 59% for 'AI Pioneers' vs 32% for others (metric label unclear)
rows.failure_or_criticism: Paid analyst reports; methodology not read. Note: the causal-AI market as defined excludes experimentation (Statsig, Eppo) and MMM spend, which look larger.

regulatory_hooks.hook: FDA final guidance: Real-World Data: Assessing EHR and Medical Claims Data (July 2024)
regulatory_hooks.rewards: fitness-for-use of RWD in regulatory studies (full PDF not read)

regulatory_hooks.hook: FDA draft guidance: Externally Controlled Trials (Feb 2023)
regulatory_hooks.rewards: protocol and SAP finalised before analysis; date-stamped justified changes; documentation of every data source considered; audit trails of data access and analyses; quantitative bias analysis; patient-level data to FDA

regulatory_hooks.hook: FDA draft guidance: AI to support regulatory decision-making for drugs and biologics (Jan 2025)
regulatory_hooks.rewards: 7-step credibility framework: context of use, model risk = influence x decision consequence, credibility plan and report; traceable, reliable data

regulatory_hooks.hook: EMA reflection paper: RWD in non-interventional studies (consultation draft 15 Apr 2024; RAPS reports adoption 17 March, article dated 8 Apr 2025)
regulatory_hooks.rewards: target-trial emulation, pre-specified sensitivity and bias analyses, negative controls, public code, registration of studies
ML admitted where the inferential guarantee holds regardless of ML quality

regulatory_hooks.hook: EU AI Act Art. 12 (automatic logs over lifetime), Art. 13 (declared accuracy level and metrics, known circumstances affecting accuracy, interpretable output)
regulatory_hooks.rewards: provenance logs and declared, conditional accuracy; Annex III dates moved to 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I to 2 Aug 2028 by a provisional Digital Omnibus deal (May 2026; final adoption not verified)

regulatory_hooks.hook: US bank model-risk guidance: SR 26-2 (17 Apr 2026, Fed/OCC/FDIC) supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8
regulatory_hooks.rewards: documentation, effective challenge, outcomes analysis/back-testing, understanding limitations, validation of vendor models; generative and agentic AI are explicitly out of scope (footnote 3)
